did.abstract: One bound volume, dated 1825, containing a copy of the Society's constitution and by-laws; meeting minutes; lists of members and officers; and accounts. Additionally, the collection includes an 1828 diploma awarded to a student.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: The bound volume was the gift of Edward Payson Ingersoll, 1896. The diploma was the gift of Seth Weber, 2024.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This small collection is housed in a single folder with no particular arrangement.

bioghist.head: Historical note
bioghist.p: The Female Union Society for the Promotion of Sabbath Schools was founded in 1816 by Joanna Graham Bethune, who along with her mother, Isabella Marshall Graham, had been longtime proponents of establishing Sunday Schools in New York City for the purpose of teaching reading and writing to impoverished children. The Society established several nondenominational Sunday schools throughout New York City that taught several thousand students.

phystech.head: Physical Characteristics and Technical Requirements
phystech.p: If digital surrogates exist, they should be used in place of the originals whenever possible.

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: Identification of item, date (if known); Female Union Society for the Promotion of Sabbath Schools records, 1973.131, Box and Folder number; Brooklyn Public Library, Center for Brooklyn History.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: This collection combines the accessions 1973.131 and 2024.041. The latter was added to the collection and the finding aid revised by Dee Bowers in November 2026.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: One bound volume, dated 1825, containing a copy of the Society's constitution and by-laws; meeting minutes; lists of members and officers; and accounts. One diploma awarded to Jane Jewson in recognition of her three years attending School No. 4, dated 1828 and signed by Joanna Bethune.
